A wanted poster — a printed-tile face nailed to a weathered brown brick post, reward-number faded, one corner curling, the outlaw already two towns gone.
A hitching-post + water-trough — a dark-tan brick rail beside a trans-blue plate trough, a rope-element looped over it, a thrown horseshoe half-buried in the dust.
A brick saguaro cactus — a tall green-brick column with two stubby upraised arms, a tiny bird-build wedged in a notch, the only shade for miles.
A tumbleweed — a loose sphere of tan flex-tube and brown bar-elements rolled against a fence post, carrying seeds from a ranch no longer on any map.
A whiskey-barrel stack — three brown brick barrels pyramided outside the saloon's side door, one tapped with a spigot-element, a spilled mug-tile dark on the boardwalk planks.
A leaning wagon-wheel — a Technic spoked wheel propped against clapboard siding, a cracked axle-element beside it, half-swallowed by a tan-plate sand drift, trip west unfinished.
A gold-pan with nuggets — a shallow grey brick pan cradling four gold 1×1 round-plate nuggets on a creek-stone, water still dripping, the prospector ran to file his claim.
A sheriff-star on the boardwalk — a gold printed-tile star face-down on grey plank-plates, dropped mid-stride, the badge lying where someone chose not to pick it back up.
An oil lantern — a trans-yellow flame stud inside a black-brick wire-frame lantern hung on a hook-element beside the stable door, still swaying from a hasty departure.
A rifle-rack — a dark-brown brick horizontal rack holding three bar-element rifle-barrels, one slot empty, the missing gun tells more than the three still hanging.
A brick campfire + coffee-pot — a ring of dark-grey brick stones with trans-orange flame elements, a black coffee-pot on an iron-bar tripod, a tin-mug tile cooling beside a bedroll.
A longhorn skull — a bleached white brick steer-skull with long curved horn-elements pressed into tan-plate desert sand, trail-marker and warning at the canyon mouth.
A dynamite-crate — an open brown brick crate with a printed danger-tile lid, red cylinder-elements packed in sawdust studs, a coiled fuse-element draped over the mine-cart rail.
A telegraph-pole — a tall brown brick pole with a crossarm and rubber-band wire sagging to the next post, the only line connecting this town to anything beyond the ridge.
A horseshoe — a single curved iron-grey brick horseshoe half-sunk in a tan plate outside the smithy, lost from a horse ridden hard through the night.
A spittoon — a small bronze-coloured round-brick vessel wedged in the saloon corner, a dark trans-brown tile inside, the least glamorous artefact of the frontier.
A saddle on a rail — a brown-brick saddle with stirrup-bar elements draped over a corral rail, a coiled lariat-element hung beside it, the rider inside settling a debt.
A hay bale — a tight yellow-brick rectangular block tied with a tan-string element, pitched off the back of a wagon, one corner already pulled loose by a mule.
A well + bucket — a grey brick well-ring with a timber-plank roof, a windlass axle-element, and a bucket on a rope-element, a dipper-tile on the rim, the only water in July.
A cattle-brand iron — a long bar-element handle with a printed-tile brand head resting in a small brick forge-bed of trans-orange coals, the herd's ownership about to be made permanent.
A sheriff-star on a nail — a gold printed-tile badge hung on a single stud-peg beside the jailhouse door, the previous owner carried out feet-first yesterday afternoon.
An oil-lantern — a trans-yellow round brick globe on a black bracket-element fixed to a boardwalk post, still lit at noon, the marshal never came home to blow it out.
A longhorn-skull — a white brick steer-skull with long curved horn-elements half-pressed into a tan-plate sand base, a trail marker that means you are already in trouble.
A hay-bale — a yellow brick rectangular bale with tan plate binding-strips beside the stable door, a pitchfork rod-element jammed upright, the stablehand nowhere to be found since supper.
A gold-pan with silt — a wide grey round-plate pan tilted on a creek-rock, brown 1×1 plate pebble-elements settled at the bottom, no nuggets today, hunger setting in by the river.
A dynamite-crate lid — a single flat brown plate stamped with a printed danger-tile lying in the mine tunnel entrance, the crate itself nowhere near where it should be.
A tumbleweed against the jail — a rod-element sphere wedged against a dark-brick jailhouse corner, the door ajar, the cell empty, the tumbleweed the only thing still in custody.
A telegraph-pole snapped — a brown brick pole broken at mid-height, the cross-arm tilted, a wire-element trailing into tan-plate dust, the next message to the marshal will not arrive.
A gold-pan + nuggets — a grey dish-plate pan holding four gold 1×1 round-plate nuggets on a creek-rock, the prospector's hands still shaking from the find.
A campfire bedroll — a tan plate bedroll beside a cold trans-orange fire-ring, a boot-element set beside it, its owner gone before the posse arrived at dawn.
A broken fence post — a snapped dark-brown brick post with a barbed-wire string-element trailing, the gap in the cattle fence that started a range war last Tuesday.
A medicine-show wagon step — a single wooden-plank brick step below a painted-tile snake-oil poster, the wagon long gone, the step left for whoever believed the pitch.
A noose on a post — a looped rope-element on a dark timber-brick crossbeam at the edge of town, a grim brick reminder that the circuit judge arrives Friday.
A miner's pickaxe + ore-chunk — a dark-grey pick-element resting against a rough rock-brick ore-chunk with a single gold-plate vein, the claim staked but the miner missing since Tuesday.
A notice-board — a tan brick post with three printed-tile notices nailed at angles, one tax notice, one land claim, one meeting cancelled, the town arguing about all three.
A boot-scraper — a dark-grey angled brick plate beside the saloon door, caked with a tan-plate mud tile, left by every rider who came in from the long drive south.
A medicine-wagon sign — a bright printed-tile board leaned against a brick wagon side, bold colour lettering, the snake-oil seller gone by morning with the takings and two horses.
A broken-down fence post — a single leaning brown brick post with a snapped bar-element, barbed-wire string draped loose, the cattle already through and three hours gone.
A canteen on a peg — a dark-tan brick canteen-build hanging from a single stud-peg outside the trading post door, half-empty, left by someone who never came back for it.
A medicine-show wagon board — a printed-tile painted sign propped on brick crates outside the abandoned wagon, bright colours, big promises, the doctor long gone with the townsfolk's coin.
A jail-cell window — a black Technic bar grid pressed into a dark-brown brick wall, a tan minifigure-hand element gripping one bar, a scratched tally-tile on the inner stone below.
A boot-hill grave marker — a brown brick cross-bar stake pressed into a sand-plate mound, a printed name-tile nailed front, a dried flower-element laid at the base, nobody left to mourn.
A prospector's pickaxe — a grey brick handle with a dark-silver axe-bar element head, leaning against a rock-face build, a fresh chip of tan plate rubble at the base, colour in that last swing.
A boot-spur — a single small grey spur-element on a saloon-plate floor beside an overturned chair, the brawl settled fast, its owner limping toward the livery stable.
A broken whiskey-bottle — a trans-brown round-tile shard cluster on a boardwalk-plate, a damp dark stain on the plank beside it, the argument that started it still unfinished.
A sheriff's notice board — a brown brick post with three printed-tile notices pinned over older ones, law older than the town, the newest one posted this morning.
A boot spur — a silver clip-and-bar spur element dropped on the saloon's dark-brown plate floor, its owner left in a hurry, chair still spinning at the table.
A stage-coach strongbox — a dark-brown brick chest with a printed lock-tile, one hinge broken open, empty, sitting in the road-plate dust two miles from the relay station.
A medicine-show cart — a small brick flatbed with a printed-tile tonic-bottle and a folded banner-element rolled tight, parked at the edge of town, the seller already gone.
A wanted poster on a post — a printed-tile bandit-face nailed to a brown brick post, reward-number faded, one corner curling, the outlaw rode through three days ago.
A hitching-post and water-trough — a brown brick rail with a trans-blue plate trough, a coiled rope-element looped over, a thrown horseshoe-tile half-buried in the tan-plate dust.
A brick campfire and coffee-pot — a ring of grey rock-plates holding trans-orange flame elements, a black round-brick coffee-pot on an iron-rod tripod, a dented tin-mug tile beside a blanket-roll.
A well and bucket — a grey brick stone-ring well with a timber-plate roof, a windlass-bar and a bucket-element on a string, a dipper-tile balanced on the rim for anyone thirsty enough to stop.
A spice-tin on a chuck-wagon shelf — a small red 1×1 tile tin clipped to a tan brick wagon shelf, the cook's only luxury on the cattle drive, guarded more fiercely than the strongbox.
A boot-scraper by the saloon door — an iron bar-element scraper set in a tan-plate step, caked with dried tan-brick mud, the only manners this town reliably enforces.
A broken-spoke wheel hub — a Technic axle-hub with two intact and two snapped spokes resting in the dust-plate behind the wheelwright's shop, waiting on parts that may never arrive.
A locked strongbox — a dark grey brick chest with a printed lock-tile hasp on a stagecoach-plate floor, a chain-element looped through a seat-bar, the payroll inside speaking for itself.
A boot outside the door — a tan brick cowboy-boot-form lying on its side on a boardwalk-plate, a spur-element still attached, its owner carried out and not walking tonight.
A mail-sack — a tan brick bag-form slumped against a brick post-office wall, a printed address-tile stitched to the front, the stage is three days late and someone inside is still waiting.
A spyglass on a fence-post — a grey-cylinder telescope element balanced on a corral stud, aimed at the ridge, whoever left it there spotted something and ran.
A medicine-wagon crate — a dark-red open brick crate with a printed-tile label, small bottle-elements inside, left by a fast-departing showman before the tar-and-feathers arrived.
A boot with a spur — a single brown-brick cowboy-boot shape with a silver-disc spur-tile, sitting upright in the dust outside the undertaker, its partner nowhere found.
A wagon-wheel leaning — a Technic spoked wheel propped against weathered grey brick planking, half-sunk in a tan-plate drift, the wagon itself long gone to splinters.
A sheriff-star pinned to a post — a gold printed-tile badge tacked to a brown brick notice-board beside three names, each crossed out, the fourth still wanted and breathing.
A canteen on a fence — a grey round-brick canteen hanging from a bar-element hook on a split-rail fence, half-full, a reminder of someone who did not come back.
A boot on a boardwalk step — a brown brick cowboy boot with a spur-element, sitting alone on a tan-plate step, one boot only, the story behind that entirely unclear.
A playing-card on the floor — a single flat printed-tile ace face-up on a dark-plate saloon floor, a chair overturned behind it in tan-plate dust, the game ended badly.
A campfire + coffee-pot — a ring of dark-grey round bricks with trans-orange flame elements, a black pot on a bar-element tripod, coffee gone cold.
A spilled-ink telegraph message — a white printed tile resting on the boardwalk planks beside the pole-base, the words that started the whole trouble.
A medicine-show sign — a printed red-and-gold tile nailed to a brick post beside an empty wagon-plate, the doctor long gone with everyone's money.
A telegraph-key desk — a tan brick shelf with a printed-tile Morse key and a paper-tile strip scrolling out, the message decoded only by the frightened operator.
A dynamite plunger — a red and grey brick detonator-box with a printed handle-element, wires trailing behind it toward the canyon wall, nobody standing close.
A bedroll + boots — a brown brick sleeping-roll beside a campfire ring, two black cylinder-boot elements set upright at the edge, owner sleeping or not, unclear.
A lockbox — a dark-grey printed-tile iron chest with a bar-element hasp, half-buried under a floorboard-plate, the combination scratched off, found during renovation.
A broken bottle — a trans-green round-stud brick bottle on its side on a boardwalk plate, contents gone, lying outside the jailhouse door after a long night.
A map tacked to a post — a printed-tile treasure-map fragment nailed to a rough brick post at the crossroads, edges torn, someone got here first.
A campfire and coffee-pot — a ring of grey 1×1 round-bricks with trans-orange flame-elements, a black container-brick pot on a bar-element tripod, one mug-tile, one man, no plans.
A hitching post and trough — a brown-brick post rail over a trans-blue plate water-trough, a clip-held rope-element looped twice, the horse gone, the rope still warm.
A saguaro cactus — a tall green-brick column with two upraised arm-bricks, a clip-held bird-build perched on the crown, the only witness to what crossed this trail at dawn.
A spilled oil-lantern — a pearl-gold globe-brick lantern tipped on tan-plate boards, trans-orange flame-tile beside it, dark scorch-plate beneath, somebody left in a very great hurry.
A longhorn-skull weathervane — a white brick skull with bar-horn elements mounted on a pole-brick atop the barn, pointing west all day, the cattle smell the storm before men do.
A broken rifle by the trail — a grey barrel-element snapped at a clip-joint, stock-brick half-buried in dust-plates, no owner nearby, the silence around it doing all the explaining.
A brand-new padlock on the safe — a dark-grey clip-and-bar lock element on a printed-tile vault door, yesterday there was no lock, today there is, the payroll arrived last night.
A canteen on a fence post — a dark-blue round-brick canteen on a clip-element fence-peg, a tan strap-bar looped over, full or empty unknown, the owner's direction equally uncertain.
A sheriff-star badge pinned to a clapboard wall — a gold printed-tile star nailed beside a wanted poster, the former owner having ridden out at dawn.
A rope lasso coiled on a post — a looped string-element lariat hung on a brown brick fence-post, stiff with dried mud, last used three days ago.
A mail-pouch on a bench — a brown plate satchel with a printed-tile postal seal, sitting on a boardwalk plank-build, nobody collected it, addressed to the dead man.
A broken lantern on the jail floor — a smashed trans-yellow plate shard with a black bracket-element frame bent open, the prisoner left in the dark on purpose.
A hitching post and water-trough — a dark-brown brick rail beside a trans-blue plate trough, a frayed rope-element looped twice, the rider hasn't returned by sundown.
A gold pan and nuggets — a grey dish-element on a creek-rock plate, four gold 1×1 round plates glinting inside, a pickaxe-element dropped close, camp empty.
A dynamite crate — a brown open-top brick crate with a printed danger-tile stencil, red cylinder dynamite-elements nestled inside, a grey coiled-chain fuse draped over the edge.
A telegraph pole — a tall stacked brown-brick pole with a printed insulator-tile cross-arm, a thread-element wire sagging toward the next pole, the line recently cut.
A rifle rack — a wall-mounted dark-grey bracket-plate holding three brown brick rifle-elements, one slot empty, a printed ammunition-tile box below, the missing rifle still warm.
A sheriff-star badge on a desk — a gold printed star-tile pinned to a tan-plate desk surface beside a written-tile deed, the new marshal hasn't touched either one.
A campsite bedroll — a rolled tan-plate cylinder secured with strap-tiles beside a saddle-bag brick build, a boot-element beside it, the owner gone before first light.
A mine-cart on rails — a dark-grey brick hopper on Technic-axle wheels set on brown rail-plate tracks, half-filled with rock-brick rubble, left at the shaft mouth mid-shift.
A noose on a beam — a looped string-element tied to a brown brick crossbeam above a trap-plate floor, a printed verdict-tile nailed to the post, the square gone quiet.
A sheriff-office cell-key — a flat-tile key hanging on a single stud hook beside a barred-plate door, the hook empty side telling half the night's story.
A trapper's fur-bale — a dark-brown brick bundle tied with a string-element, stacked on a dock-plate beside the trading post, worth a winter's silence and cold.
A bounty-hunter's saddlebag — two dark-brown stud-closed plate pouches clipped over a rail, a printed-tile wanted-poster corner visible inside, the hunter somewhere very close.
A hitching post and water trough — a tan brick rail with a trans-blue plate trough, a coiled rope-element looped over, hoofprints pressed into the tan-plate dust beside it.
A gold pan with nuggets — a grey dish-element cradling three gold 1×1 round-plate nuggets, resting on a creek-rock stack, a claim-stake tile driven beside it.
A sheriff star on the boardwalk — a gold printed-tile star dropped between two dark-brown plank-plates, face-down, nobody reaching to pick it up this morning.
A brick campfire and coffee pot — a ring of grey rock-elements cupping trans-orange flame tiles, a black pot on an iron-rod tripod, a tin-mug tile beside a brown bedroll.
A boot-hill marker — a rough dark-grey brick cross driven into tan-plate earth, a single printed-tile name barely legible, a hat-element laid at the base and not retrieved.
A broken-down stagecoach door — a hinged dark-brown plate door leaning against a brick-wall section, a bullet-hole printed tile through the window, the passengers made it, the driver did not.
A telegraph-office waste-pile — a grey brick bin stuffed with folded-paper-tile message slips outside the office window, the urgent ones still undelivered, the operator nowhere to be found.
A mine-cart — a dark-grey brick open-top cart on rail-plate tracks, loaded with two gold 1×1 round plates and a pickaxe-element, abandoned mid-haul at the tunnel mouth.
A broken-fence post — a snapped tan brick fencepost with a loose barbed-wire bar dangling from a clip-element, the cattle already through the gap and into someone else's corn.
A deputy's badge + handcuffs — a printed silver-tile star beside a cuff-element chain on the jailhouse desk-plate, both left behind; the deputy rode out alone at first light.
A canteen on a rock — a tan brick rounded flask with a cork-element stopper resting on a grey-plate boulder at the crossroads, still half-full, its owner not coming back for it.
A whiskey barrel stack — a pyramid of brown brick barrels outside the saloon, one tapped with a spigot-element, a spilled mug-tile flat on the boardwalk planks.
A well with bucket — a brick stone well-ring with a log-element windlass, a bucket on a rope-element, dipper-tile balanced on the rim, the town depends on it.
A wagon wheel leaning — a Technic spoked wheel propped against a weathered grey brick wall, half-buried in a tan-plate dust drift, the wagon it belonged to never arrived.
A spade in the dirt — a grey brick shovel blade with a bar-element handle jammed into a brown stud-plate soil patch, the grave outline already scratched around it.
A broken whiskey bottle — a trans-brown round brick bottle on its side between two boardwalk plates, contents tile-puddled around it, the argument that caused it still unresolved.
A medicine-show bottle crate — an open tan brick crate of coloured 1×1 round-plate bottles left behind a wagon, the Professor departed fast and the cure is purely fictional.
A branding-fire pit — a shallow brick-lined stone pit with trans-orange flame elements and two bar-element irons crossed above it, the herd count chalked on a plank beside it.
A miner's pickaxe — a dark grey bar-element handle with a printed-tile axe head propped against a mine-cart, one strike chipped out a gold stud that changed everything.
A hitching post + water-trough — a brown-brick rail beside a trans-blue plate trough, a coiled rope-element looped over, a horseshoe pressed into the tan-plate dust.
A boot-knife in a board — a small blade-element stuck into a thick plank-plate at the saloon threshold, left there by the last man asked to disarm.
A miner's canteen — a flat dark-grey brick canteen-build with a stopper-stud resting on a boulder-plate, half-empty, beside a trail marker pointing toward the silver hills.
A broken-chain shackle — two dark-grey ring-link elements separated at one joint, lying on a dusty tan-plate ground tile, someone made it out of the jailhouse.
A brick campfire with coffee-pot — a ring of grey round-plate stones, trans-orange flame elements rising, a black pot on crossed bar-element tripod legs, breakfast burning.
A hitching-post with water-trough — a brown brick rail post with a trans-blue plate trough below, a string-element rope looped tight, three horses expected back by sundown.
A gold-scale on a counter — a grey bracket-element balance-arm with two dish-plate pans, a few 1×1 round-plate gold nuggets on one side, dispute pending.
A tin-star pinboard — a brown brick board studded with printed deputy-tile stars in various sizes, two pins empty, two men short in a dangerous week.
A rope-coil on a fence-post — a tan string-element lasso coiled on a single brown brick post, knot already tied, someone in this town is very angry.
A medicine-wagon step — two brick steps with a printed snake-oil-tile sign leaning against them, the wagon itself long gone, only the promise left behind.
A brick saguaro — two raised-arm green brick columns beside the mesa-plate trail, a tiny bird-stud perched on top, the only witness to what passed here.
A hitching-post with trough — a brown brick rail and a trans-blue plate water-trough, rope-element looped over once, the horse that was tied here gone without the rider.
A campfire with coffee-pot — a ring of grey-plate stones with trans-orange flame elements, a black brick coffee-pot on a bar-element tripod, tin-mug tile cooling, camp abandoned quickly.
A spyglass on a rock — a tan-plate mesa-rock with a cylinder-element brass telescope resting on it, cap-tile beside it, whoever was watching the valley floor left in a hurry.
A lockbox with coins — a small dark-brown brick strongbox, padlock-bar element snapped open, a scatter of gold 1×1 coin-tiles on the plank-plate floor, the safe already emptied.
A boot-print trail — a sequence of dark-tan 1×1 round-plates pressed into a sand-plate floor leading toward the livery, one set going in, no prints coming back out.
A lantern on a grave-marker — a trans-yellow flame-brick inside a wire-element cage hung from a simple cross built of brown bricks, someone keeping a vigil nobody else bothered to keep.
A gold-claim stake — a pointed brown brick post with a printed title-tile deed nailed on, a pick-element and a measuring-rope beside it, driven hard into a creek-bank at first light.
